title: Grow a Rock: shipping an AI-assisted incremental destruction game with a free browser demo
author: oddgustudio
selftext:
I’m the developer behind dorivoltgames, and I’ve released Grow a Rock. You grow a tiny pebble, buy upgrades with ore, then roll it through obstacles. Early on, an acorn stops you. Later, the same rock can flatten vending machines and buildings. The rolling sections include jumps and downward slams.



For this community, the useful part to share is where AI fitted into development. It was used across code review and fixes, art, music and localization. One concrete example on the code side was refining input/jump handling and collision behaviour. Those changes still needed testing against the actual rolling sections; a change that makes an input register is only part of getting the game to feel responsive. Recent work has also included clearer gameplay/UI feedback.



The browser demo covers the first two areas for free, roughly 25 minutes. There are no ads, and English and Korean are supported. The full game is paid, and I’m preparing more content.



Play the free browser demo: [https://dorivoltgames.itch.io/grow-a-rock](https://dorivoltgames.itch.io/grow-a-rock)

Gameplay trailer: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=77c0YwID8U0](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=77c0YwID8U0)

Full game ($2.99): [https://dorivoltgames.itch.io/grow-a-rock-full](https://dorivoltgames.itch.io/grow-a-rock-full)

Android / ONE store: [https://onesto.re/0001010958](https://onesto.re/0001010958)



AI disclosure: AI was used for code review, debugging and implementing code fixes that are included in the game; image/art assets in the game and promotional materials; and background music. Gameplay sound effects are synthesized procedurally by the game’s audio code, with AI assistance in the audio/code workflow. AI was also used for translation/localization, game/store/promotional text and this post, QA/test scripts, build/release utilities and technical troubleshooting.



If you try it, I’d be interested in whether the jump/slam controls feel responsive and whether the growth is clear without watching the numbers. Those are the parts I’m continuing to tune.
